title: Axion-Like Inflaton Coupling Could Produce Heavy Neutrinos Explaining
excerpt: Theoretical physicists model how axion-like inflaton couplings generate heavy right-handed neutrinos during inflation and preheating to explain cosmic baryon asymmetry.
content:
Theoretical physicists have developed a unified theoretical framework investigating the production of heavy right-handed neutrinos driven by derivative couplings to an axion-like inflaton. The theoretical study explores the direct cosmological implications of these interactions for non-thermal leptogenesis, focusing on Majorana-fermion production mechanisms across distinct early-universe evolutionary phases spanning cosmic inflation and subsequent preheating.

During the inflationary phase, the rolling axion-like inflaton background dynamically generates a helicity-asymmetric spectrum of heavy fermions. The researchers showed that this spectrum can be obtained analytically in the slow-roll regime.

As the cosmic evolution enters preheating, the oscillating inflaton background drives repeated non-adiabatic production events. These production events feature a helicity-dependent effective momentum and a natural momentum cutoff.

The investigators calculated the net particle abundance across both delayed-decay and prompt-decay limiting cases. Their calculations incorporate the quantum effects of Pauli blocking and account for successive production stages throughout the oscillating background. Additionally, the analysis clarifies the mathematical relationship connecting the fermion basis used to identify non-adiabatic production with the Hamiltonian-diagonal basis defining instantaneous particle occupation numbers.

Applying these results to non-thermal leptogenesis, the researchers identified parameter regions consistent with the observed baryon asymmetry.

Subject of Research: Theoretical physics of neutrino production during cosmic inflation and leptogenesis

Article Title: Right-handed neutrino production by an axion-like inflaton: implications for leptogenesis
